terms.meaning: Pulling a small sample's estimate toward a broader average, so one unusual result does not dominate.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and constants
sections.what: Explains that the script builds option counts from the same training seasons as the outcome model, and notes where bowling styles come from. It also sets the shrinkage value and minimum count.
sections.why: The header records the source and the reason for not guessing styles.
sections.watch_out: The minimum count and shrinkage values decide how cautious the Decision Lab is, so changing them changes what it will grade.

sections.name: styleClass
sections.title: Bowling style labels
sections.what: Turns a free-text bowling style label into pace, spin, or nothing, based on keywords.
sections.why: Labels are free text, so keyword matching turns them into two usable groups.
sections.watch_out: Spin keywords are checked first, and any unrecognised label stays unlabelled rather than being guessed.

sections.name: loadStyles
sections.title: Loading bowling styles
sections.what: Reads the bowling styles file and returns a map from bowler name to pace or spin, keeping only names that appear once.
sections.why: The ball data names bowlers rather than giving register ids, so a shared name cannot be matched reliably. The code drops those names.
sections.watch_out: If the file is missing the map is empty, so the run continues without styles and only the flag shows it.

sections.name: buildOptions
sections.title: Building the option counts
sections.what: Checks the data licences, loads the styles, labels each training chase situation with its options and outcome, and builds the counts.
sections.why: Keeps the counts tied to the seasons the outcome model was trained on.
sections.watch_out: The file reads outcome model settings, so the script fails if fit-outcomes has not been run first.

summary: Counts how often each decision option was tried in each game situation, using the training seasons, so the Decision Lab knows how much data supports each choice.
purpose: Creates the option counts used to grade decision types and to decide whether a decision has enough data.
why: Decisions need a baseline of what has happened before. Shrinkage and a minimum count stop small samples from looking reliable.
how: Reads the training seasons from the outcome model file, checks that the licences allow the data, loads bowling styles if the file exists, labels each chase situation with its options and outcome, then counts them.
inputs: data/models/outcomes-v1.json for training seasons, the chase ball data, and data/derived/bowling-styles.csv if present.
outputs: data/models/options-v1.json with the counts, shrinkage and minimum count settings, a flag for whether styles were used, and a fingerprint.
risks: If the styles file is missing, the pace or spin labels are simply absent, which changes the options without an error.
debug: If the output has no counts, check that the outcome model file exists and lists training seasons. If option labels look wrong, check the bowling style keywords and the styles file. Confirm the licence check passes.
